title: Solo vs Sólo: Does “Only” Need an Accent?
seo_title: Solo vs Sólo: Does “Only” Need an Accent?
meta_description: Solo vs sólo: the current RAE rule, when an accent is allowed, how to say “alone” and “only”, and how to avoid ambiguity, with examples and a quiz.
excerpt: The rule changed, and many people still argue about it. Here is what to write today.

body_html:
Solo vs sólo is the accent question that Spanish speakers themselves argue about. The word solo has two meanings: as an adjective it means “alone” (Vivo solo, I live alone), and as an adverb it means “only” (Solo quiero agua, I only want water). For decades, the adverb was written sólo with an accent. Today the Real Academia Española recommends writing solo without an accent in both cases, and allows the accent only when a sentence could genuinely be read both ways.

Quick answer
  • Solo = alone (adjective): Estoy solo en casa.
  • Solo = only (adverb): Solo tengo diez pesos.
  • The RAE recommends no accent in either case.
  • If a sentence is ambiguous, you may use sólo for “only”, or better, rephrase with solamente.
{{toc}}

Solo vs sólo: what the rule says today

Here is the short history. In 2010, the RAE and the other Spanish language academies decided that the accent on the adverb solo was no longer necessary, because context almost always shows the meaning. Many writers, teachers and newspapers disagreed and kept using it. In 2023, the RAE clarified its position: the recommended spelling is still solo without an accent, but writers may add the accent on the adverb when they see a real risk of ambiguity.

So both of these are acceptable in an ambiguous sentence, but the first is the recommended norm:

  • Trabaja solo los domingos.
  • Trabaja sólo los domingos. (only on Sundays)

You can check the current guidance in the RAE’s Diccionario panhispánico de dudas.

Solo meaning “alone”

As an adjective, solo agrees in gender and number with the noun:

  • Mi abuelo vive solo. My grandfather lives alone.
  • Mi abuela vive sola. My grandmother lives alone.
  • Los niños se quedaron solos. The children were left alone.
  • Me gusta el café solo. I like my coffee black. (In Spain, un café solo is an espresso.)

This form never takes an accent, under any rule.

{{image:2}}

Solo meaning “only”

As an adverb, solo means “only” or “just”, and it never changes form:

  • Solo quiero dormir. I just want to sleep.
  • Tengo solo dos hermanos. I have only two siblings.
  • Solo te pido una cosa. I’m only asking you for one thing.

Synonyms that always work: solamente and únicamente. In Mexico you will also hear nomás in relaxed speech: Nomás tengo dos hermanos.

How to avoid ambiguity

Real ambiguity is rare, but it happens:

Voy solo al cine. This could mean “I go to the movies alone” or “I only go to the movies”.

A translator’s solution is not to argue about the accent but to rephrase:

  • Voy al cine solo. or Voy al cine sin compañía. I go to the movies alone.
  • Solamente voy al cine. or Lo único que hago es ir al cine. I only go to the movies.

This is my own habit when translating: if a sentence could be read two ways, I rewrite it. It is clearer for every reader, whichever spelling rule they learned.

{{book:a-road-in-bloom}}

Este, ese, aquel: the same story

The demonstrative pronouns had the same rule change. People used to write éste, ése and aquél with an accent when they stood alone as pronouns: Quiero éste. Today the recommended spelling is without an accent in every case: Quiero este. See {{link:este-ese-aquel|este, ese, aquel}} for how to use them.

What I recommend to learners

If you are learning Spanish today, write solo without an accent. It is the current recommendation, it is what modern dictionaries and most publishers use, and nobody will mark it as a mistake. If you learned the old rule and prefer sólo, you will still see it in many books and some newspapers, so don’t be surprised by either form when reading.

What matters far more than the accent is agreement. Learners often forget that “alone” changes for gender and number, which is a real grammar mistake: Mis hijas están solas en casa, not “solo”. Focus your attention there.

{{image:3}}

Quick tip for typing

Whatever rule you follow, make it easy to type Spanish accents. On a phone, press and hold a vowel to see accented letters. On a Mac, hold the key down; on Windows, add the United States-International keyboard.

Practice sentences

  1. I live alone.
  2. I only have five minutes.
  3. The girls stayed home alone.
  4. I just want to rest.

Answers: 1. Vivo solo or Vivo sola. 2. Solo tengo cinco minutos. 3. Las niñas se quedaron solas en casa. 4. Solo quiero descansar.

Common mistakes

  • Ella vive sólo. Two problems: “alone” never takes an accent, and it must agree: Ella vive sola.
  • Solos quiero dos. As “only”, it never changes form: Solo quiero dos.
  • Marking someone wrong for writing sólo. The accented adverb is outdated but not a serious error, and it is allowed in ambiguous cases.

For the accent rules that have not changed, such as {{link:si-vs-si|si vs sí}} and {{link:el-vs-el|el vs él}}, see {{link:spanish-accent-marks|Spanish accent marks}}.

{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

Solo vs sólo is a good reminder that languages change. Write solo without an accent, make it agree when it means “alone”, and rephrase with solamente if a sentence could be misread. For other pairs that confuse learners, see {{link:spanish-confusing-words|Spanish confusing words}}.

faq.q: Does solo have an accent in Spanish?
faq.a: The RAE recommends writing solo without an accent, both for “alone” and “only”. An accent on the adverb is allowed only when a sentence is genuinely ambiguous.
Not exactly. It is no longer the recommended spelling, but it is accepted for the adverb in ambiguous contexts.

faq.q: How do I say “I live alone” in Spanish?
faq.a: Vivo solo if you are male, vivo sola if you are female.

faq.q: What is the safest way to say “only”?
faq.a: Use solamente or únicamente if you want to avoid any doubt.

quiz.title: Quick quiz: solo, sola or sólo?

questions.explain: As “alone”, it agrees with a feminine subject: sola.
As “only”, it never changes. The recommended spelling has no accent.

questions.q: What does the RAE recommend for “only”?
questions.explain: No accent, with an optional accent only in ambiguous sentences.

questions.q: A synonym for “only” that is never ambiguous:
questions.explain: Solamente always means “only”. Soledad means loneliness.

questions.q: In Spain, un café solo is…
questions.explain: In Spain, café solo is black coffee, an espresso.
